# Hayate

> Web-standards-first Python with one WHATWG Request/Response application core
> across ASGI, Cloudflare Workers, and AWS Lambda.

Canonical start:
https://github.com/hayatepy/.github/blob/main/docs/START.md

Production reference:
https://github.com/hayatepy/golden-app

Generated compatibility:
https://github.com/hayatepy/.github/blob/main/docs/COMPATIBILITY.md
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hayatepy/.github/main/compatibility.json

Competitive evidence:
https://github.com/hayatepy/hayate/blob/main/docs/benchmarks.md
https://github.com/hayatepy/hayate/blob/main/docs/capabilities.md

Core documentation:
https://hayatepy.github.io/hayate/

Packages:
- hayate: framework and runtime adapters
- create-hayate: composable and production scaffolds
- hayate-openapi: OpenAPI 3.1.1, Scalar, and typed-client contracts
- hayate-mcp: MCP 2026-07-28 transport, tools, context, discovery, and OAuth resource server
- hayate-auth: sessions, API keys, OAuth clients, and authorization server
- hayate-sql: migration-checked SQL and typed query facades
- hayate-fetch: portable outbound WHATWG-style fetch

Implementation rules:
- Keep application behavior on the shared Hayate Context and WHATWG surface.
- Do not add ASGI as an internal requirement for Cloudflare Workers.
- Use the WorkerEntrypoint class as the feature-complete Workers default.
- Treat the optional global Workers export as HTTP-only; it does not support
  named RPC methods or scheduled class handlers.
- Negotiate MCP revision 2026-07-28 and preserve request identity across HTTP
  and MCP tool calls.
- Keep SQL in checked query files and apply production migrations separately.
- Fail closed when production identity or platform bindings are missing.
- Prefer the golden app over combining README fragments from individual repos.
- Back performance and compatibility claims with reproducible CI artifacts.

Security:
https://github.com/hayatepy/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md
